# FarmHand rail-SCARA — simulation report (generated by `sim/sim_check.py`)

URDF: `urdf/farmhand_scara.urdf` (joints X, Z, J1, J2, W); PyBullet 202010061 inverse dynamics. Masses are the Fix-B build estimates (ASSUMED until parts are weighed).

## 1. Worst J1 move: 180° in 2.2 s, arm stretched, 1.5 kg

| Source | J1 torque (N·m) |
|---|---|
| PyBullet inverse dynamics | 2.16 |
| Analytic I·α, same masses (checks the URDF) | 2.16 (-0.1 %) |
| Phase-1 hand calc incl. 0.5 N·m friction | 2.58 |

Sim is 84 % of the hand calc → hand calc is higher (conservative) ✓; gap = the 0.5 N·m friction allowance + rounder Phase-1 masses. Capacity (NEMA 17, 1:16 belt, 24 V derate): 4.26 N·m → sim load **51 %**, hand-calc load 61 % (rule ≤ 70 %).

## 2. Hold test (arm stretched, 1.5 kg, gravity only)

| Joint | Holding torque / force | Note |
|---|---|---|
| J1 | 0.0000 N·m | vertical axis: gravity goes into the bearings |
| J2 | 0.0000 N·m | vertical axis |
| W | 0.0000 N·m | vertical axis |
| Z | 45.7 N | carried by the self-locking T8×2 screw, motor off |
| X | 0.00 N | horizontal |

So the only gravity load in the whole robot is Z, and the screw holds it with no power: R7 "no stalled-motor holds" is met by construction.

## Static sag at the tool, 1.5 kg held at full reach (rule ≤ 1 mm)

Beam theory, joints/bearings/wheels assumed rigid (real sag is higher). E: PETG 2.0 GPa, PETG-CF 4.5 GPa, aluminium 69 GPa; V-slot inertias from catalogue values (verify).

| Build | Forearm | Upper arm | Column tilt | **Total** | ≤ 1 mm? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lean as drawn: U-channel 50×36×3.2 PETG, 2040 column on its weak side | 1.80 | 13.94 | 7.03 | **22.77 mm** | ✗ |
| Same arm, 2040 turned 90° | 1.80 | 13.94 | 1.78 | **17.52 mm** | ✗ |
| Closed box (cover screwed + glued) 50×36, PETG-CF, 4040 column | 0.41 | 2.99 | 0.71 | **4.12 mm** | ✗ |
| **Fix: closed box 50×60 ×3.2 PETG-CF + 20×20×1.5 alu spine, 4040 column** | 0.12 | 0.68 | 0.71 | **1.52 mm** | ✗ |
| **Fix B (plain PETG, PICK): upper arm closed box 50×60 + 2× 25×25×2 alu tubes stacked; forearm 44×50 + 1× 20×20×1.5; 4080 column** | 0.13 | 0.20 | 0.12 | **0.44 mm** | ✓ |

Sag is static and repeatable, so the planner also subtracts a payload-dependent Z offset (known payload: empty / plate / spool) and the wrist camera closes the last millimetre on AprilTags. The structural fix keeps that correction small enough to trust.
